content: I actually found it easier to get to this screw from the right side.  YMMV
The black point: There stands Screws. I think it must be Screw. I was looking for the second one...

The description of turning the printer could be a bit clearer. I put the printer on it's side with the left side facing up, but now I'm realizing that I was probably only supposed to spin it 90 degrees on its base (or in my case, just walk to the other side of it since it's on a corner).

replies.content: Also while it was on its side an M3 nut fell out, so hopefully that wasn't doing anything important...

content: again this screw called for a t10

replies.content:
It should have been an M3x10. At least mine was. However, a T10 will generally turn a 2.5mm hex, but not a good idea if you have to use real torque.

That said: the included T10 driver is more convenient here, as long as you don't strip it out trying to turn the screw.

content: Rather than only releasing the five cable straps, I recommend rewording this to "Remove the five cable straps".
I would remove the two "smokey" plastic top side panels during this step. I had an easier time with unscrewing things on the nextruder.
